metas.name: Breakdowns of 1938
metas.description: Flubs and bloopers that occurred on the set of some of the major Warner Bros. pictures of 1938.

metas.name: Any Bonds Today?
metas.description: Bugs Bunny and friends sing and dance to promote the sale of government bonds in support of the war effort.

metas.name: Point Rationing of Foods
metas.description: Animated documentary short film demonstrating the reasons and methods of the point system of wartime food rationing.

metas.name: Coming!! Snafu
metas.description: Introducing Private Snafu, the nation's worst soldier and his various versions in different branches of the armed forces. The cartoon, ironic and humorous in tone, was created during World War II and it was designed to instruct service personnel about security, proper sanitation habits, booby traps

metas.name: Mopping Up
metas.description: A Terrytoon cartoon.

metas.name: Spies
metas.description: The doltish but self-confident and self-congratulatory Private Snafu is in possession of a military secret during World War II. Over the course of the day, spouting rhymed couplets, he divulges the secret a little at a time to listening Axis spies. He tells his mom some of the secret when he calls h

metas.name: The Gold Brick
metas.description: A fairy encourages Snafu to duck out of his training regime for his own reasons.

metas.name: The Infantry Blues
metas.description: Pvt. Snafu complains about being assigned to the infantry only to learn that other branches have their own problems.

metas.name: Fighting Tools
metas.description: Pvt. Snafu suffers the consequences of not keeping his equipment and weapons properly maintained.

metas.name: The Home Front
metas.description: A homesick Pvt. Snafu learns that his family are almost as committed to the war efforts as himself.

metas.name: Rumors
metas.description: Snafu inadvertantly starts a panic on his base when he begins a mistaken rumour that the base is about to be bombed.

metas.name: Going Home
metas.description: Pvt. Snafu's unit suffers the consequences of blabbing military secrets while on leave at home.

metas.name: Booby Traps
metas.description: Pvt. Snafu thinks he's too smart to get caught by an enemy booby trap, but he soon finds that the traps are alluring and that he is every bit the booby.

metas.name: Snafuperman
metas.description: Pvt. Snafu becomes a superhero, only for him to become the world's dumbest one because he won't study his field manuals.

metas.name: Private Snafu vs. Malaria Mike
metas.description: Snafu learns hard way the consequences of not protecting himself from malaria infection.

metas.name: A Lecture on Camouflage
metas.description: Using Snafu as an example, Techanical Fairy First Class teaches the methods of effective camouflage.

metas.name: Gas
metas.description: Snafu learns the need of keeping his gas mask at hand when he is attacked by anthropomorphic gas cloud.

metas.name: The Chow Hound
metas.description: Snafu learns of the folly of hoarding and wasting military food supplies.

metas.name: Censored
metas.description: Private Snafu wants to tell his sweetheart, Sally Lou, that he thinks his unit will be sent to the South Pacific. But every effort he makes to get his letter through uncensored is thwarted by a resourceful (and unseen) censor with an array of contraptions and booby traps. Not even Snafu's carrier pi

metas.name: Outpost
metas.description: Snafu has an object lesson on the value of complete and accurate regular reports when he discovers and reports evidence of the enemy's presence at his assigned area.

metas.name: Pay Day
metas.description: Technical Fairy First Class shows Snafu the consequences of frittering away his pay.

metas.name: Three Brothers
metas.description: Dissatisfied with being assigned to shoe consignment detail, Snafu learns about the true value of his responsibilities

metas.name: Target Snafu
metas.description: An armada of malaria-laden mosquitoes seeks human targets and finds Private Snafu, who fails to protect himself adequately against their onslaught.

metas.name: In the Aleutians
metas.description: A humourous look at the Aleutian Islands and their strategic value.

metas.name: It's Murder She Says...
metas.description: A haggard mosquito complains how tough life is with the military taking the proper precautions against malaria infection.

metas.name: Hot Spot
metas.description: As the Devil watches Pvt. Snafu and his unit stationed in Iran, he talks about the hazards of working in the heat.

metas.name: Operation Snafu
metas.description: Private Snafu steals secret Japanese war plans, is captured and tried.  He escapes and rows out to sea.

metas.name: No Buddy Atoll
metas.description: Private Snafu is stranded on a tiny island with a Japanese officer; he must depend on his wits to defend himself against his sword-wielding foe.

metas.name: Tokyo Woes
metas.description: Created for the US Navy in World War II. The Mr. Hook character was created by Hank Ketcham while at Walter Lantz Studios, where the first- and only color- Mr. Hook cartoon was produced. A wartime propaganda film about Japan and war bonds. The loudspeaker grille is in the shape of a peace sign as it

metas.name: The Good Egg
metas.description: Navy seaman Mr. Hook is convinced of the value of holding on to his war bonds.

metas.name: The Return of Mr. Hook
metas.description: Seaman Hook has big plans for after the war, mostly involving rushing home and marrying his sweetie. So do his fellow seaman, but theirs involve buying bonds.

metas.name: Private Snafu Presents Seaman Tarfu in the Navy
metas.description: Private Snafu (Situation Normal  All Fucked Up)  presents his brother Tarfu (Things Are Really Fucked Up) who was a carrier pigeon keeper and has joined the Navy

metas.name: So Much for So Little
metas.description: Little Johnny Jones, to be born in the next year, is shown growing to a ripe, healthy old age, thanks to the efforts of his local public health officers. metas.name: Drafty, Isn't It?
metas.description: Ralph Phillips dreams about his future, only to have his dreams interrupted by Willie N. List, using an ACME Anti-Nightmare Machine, to compare military and civilian life.
